inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 191.637M shares on the Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover (24 Aug 2026) plus 0.78M dilutive equity-award equivalents from the Q3 EPS note (weighted diluted 192.319M). Already includes the NVIDIA private placement shares and is net of the $300M repurchased in 9M FY2026. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: the company is in net debt (6.4bn), so there is no cash pile added back to EV. 9M FY2026 interest income was only 48.8M. The forward flows are unlevered (built from EBITDA), so neither interest income nor the ~560M/yr interest expense is in them; the debt is charged once, through net_debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026E. SBC expense: 9M FY2026 cash-flow add-back 712.6M (Q3 10-Q) + ~235M for Q4 at the Q2/Q3 run-rate = ~948M (9.8% of revenue). Equity-award taxes: 'Payments for taxes related to net share settlement of equity awards' 262.8M for 9M, ~325M full-year on the FY2025 seasonal pattern (9M 242.8M -> FY 305.5M). Synopsys publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule. See notes: for this company the sum is probably conservative.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 financing-activity outflow (Purchases of treasury stock). Buybacks were zero in FY2024 and FY2025 while the Ansys deal was funded; resumed Feb 2026 under a replenished $2.0bn authorisation (authorised, not spent). The flat count is therefore only partly funded so far.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (US 10-year), ERP 4.6%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.4%. Debt is ~10% of capital (10.0bn of mostly fixed-rate senior notes against ~88bn of equity) at ~5% pre-tax, ~4% after tax -> WACC ~9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the scenario weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (804M of liabilities, US GAAP) stay inside operating expense and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; they are NOT in net_debt. One treatment only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, routed via dcf-methods as a US software operating company (EDA + semiconductor IP + Ansys simulation). Fresh build, no prior valuation. BASE YEAR: FY0 is FY2026 (ended 31 Oct 2026) on 9M actuals plus the Q4 guide raised at Q3 earnings: revenue 9.69-9.74bn (midpoint 9,715 = 7,161.6 actual 9M + ~2,555 guided Q4), non-GAAP operating margin ~41.5%, FCF ~2.6bn, capex ~225M. FY2026 actuals are due 8 Dec 2026 and should replace these. This is the first full year of the post-Ansys, post-Software-Integrity, post-Optical-Solutions business, so growth and margins are built from it and NOT from the FY2021-FY2025 history, which mixes a divested segment in and has only 3.5 months of Ansys in FY2025. ADJ EBITDA MARGIN: 43.6% = guided 41.5% non-GAAP operating margin + ~2.1% of revenue of ordinary depreciation and amortisation (9M total D&A 1,362.0M less 1,210.3M of acquired-intangible amortisation = 151.7M, ~203M annualised). It excludes SBC (charged separately), acquired-intangible amortisation (~1.6bn/yr, non-cash and largely non-deductible on a stock deal), restructuring (236M charged in 9M; plan total 425-500M through FY2027) and deal costs. D&A path therefore carries ordinary D&A only. CASH TAX: 23% of post-SBC EBIT. Synopsys's non-GAAP normalised rate is ~16%, but that is levied on a pre-SBC base; cash taxes paid were 512.7M in FY2025 and 680.1M in FY2024, and against an EBIT that deducts 13% of revenue for equity compensation the unlevered cash rate works out in the low-to-mid 20s. Held flat; no valuation-allowance benefit is carried forward. SBC CAVEAT: the house rule sums the SBC expense (9.8% of revenue) and the cash paid for withholding taxes on net-share settlement (3.3%), giving 13.1%. For Synopsys this looks conservative: in 9M FY2026 the count excluding the NVIDIA placement and buybacks rose ~0.75% (~640M at the current price) and withholding taxes were 263M, about 900M in total, close to the 948M SBC expense alone. The path glides from 12.7% to 9.0%, i.e. to today's expense-only level. The house/street band shows how much the answer depends on this. NET DEBT is as at 31 July 2026; Q4 FY2026 free cash flow (~460M implied by the 2.6bn guide less 2,142.5M for 9M, before any Q4 buybacks) is not credited, worth roughly $2 per share. YEAR-1 CHECK: FY2026 underlying unlevered owner FCF is ~2.0bn (2,600 reported + ~450 after-tax interest + ~260 after-tax restructuring and deal cash - 1,273 equity comp), a 21% margin; the base case year-1 figure is ~2.4bn at ~23%, the step being 9.5% growth plus the first full year of the ~10% headcount reduction. HISTORY: reported FCF and SBC are XBRL as filed; FY2021 and earlier revenue include Software Integrity, FY2022-FY2024 are restated continuing operations.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward organic growth of the continuing post-Ansys business (FY2027 base case); historical CAGRs are not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (72% 3-yr) diverges from revenue (15%) and EPS (9%) by far more than 30pp: equity went from 5.5bn to 28.3bn because ~18bn of stock was issued for Ansys in July 2025. It measures deal consideration, not compounding, and is rejected as a growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 and FY2020->FY2025 on reported annual figures. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income additionally stripped in FY2024 when net cash was 3.9bn): FY2020 505.8, FY2022 969.3, FY2023 709.0, FY2024 170.7, FY2025 150.4, FY2026E 1,327. Owner FCF fell while reported FCF was roughly flat because equity compensation (expense plus withholding taxes) rose from 331M in FY2020 to 1,199M in FY2025, and because FY2024-FY2025 carry deal financing costs, 680M and 513M of cash taxes (the FY2024 figure includes tax on the Software Integrity gain) and only a part-year of Ansys. The FY2020 revenue base includes Software Integrity, so the 5-year revenue CAGR understates continuing-operations growth; FY2025 and FY2026E revenue are inflated by Ansys (FY2026E growth of 38% is almost entirely acquired). None of these series describes the business as it now stands.

base.rationale: Growth: EDA (60% of revenue) at low double digits as guided, Ansys at high single to low double digits, Design IP (25% pre-divestiture, now less after the Processor IP sale) at low-to-mid single digits; blended ~10%, fading from year 6. Backlog slipped from 11.4bn to 10.9bn over 9M FY2026, which is why the base case does not go above 10%. Margin: adjusted EBITDA from 43.6% to 47.5%, i.e. a non-GAAP operating margin of ~45.5%, on the restructuring savings and Ansys cost synergies. Working capital: small positive capture; deferred revenue rose 116M in 9M FY2026 but was offset by inventories and long-term contract assets.

scenario_narratives.base: AI and high-performance-computing design starts keep core EDA growing at low double digits, as management guided for FY2026, and the Synopsys-Cadence duopoly holds its pricing. Ansys grows a little slower than EDA, with cross-selling into the semiconductor base arriving gradually rather than as a step. Design IP recovers only to low-to-mid single-digit growth: the roadmap reset helps, but China export controls and the weak foundry customer persist. Revenue compounds ~10% for four years and fades to 4.5% by year 10. The FY2026 restructuring and Ansys cost synergies lift the non-GAAP operating margin from 41.5% to ~45.5%, and equity compensation eases from 13% to 9% of revenue as the enlarged revenue base outgrows headcount. Debt is serviced comfortably and is charged once, through net debt.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI design supercycle broadens from a handful of hyperscaler and GPU programmes into multi-die, chiplet and custom-silicon work across the industry, and agentic AI tools (Synopsys.ai) are priced as engineering capacity rather than seats, lifting EDA growth into the mid-teens. The 'silicon to systems' thesis works: joint EDA-plus-simulation products and the NVIDIA partnership pull Ansys growth into the low teens, and the refocused IP portfolio (interconnect, HBM, UCIe) returns to high single-digit growth. Revenue compounds 12-13% through year 4. Scale and synergies take the adjusted EBITDA margin to 50%, in line with Cadence's profitability, and equity compensation falls to 8.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI design-start growth normalises and customers consolidate tool spend; EDA slows to mid single digits. Design IP keeps shrinking in real terms as the roadmap reset fails to win back share and the foundry customer does not recover. A renewed US export-control action cuts off a large part of China revenue for good and accelerates state-backed domestic EDA substitution. Ansys integration disappoints: channel partners and key staff leave, cross-sell does not appear, and restructuring becomes a recurring cost rather than a one-off, so margins slip to 42.5% instead of expanding. Equity compensation stays above 11% of revenue to retain engineers. Growth runs 5-6% and fades to 3%. The business remains solidly cash generative and the debt is serviceable; this is a de-rating case, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: Design IP has already missed once (and is the subject of consolidated securities litigation), China exposure is subject to abrupt regulatory action that has already happened once, and the Ansys integration is still inside its first eighteen months with 10bn of debt outstanding. Base 50%: it is essentially management's own FY2026 trajectory extended, supported by 10.9bn of backlog. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30%: it needs three largely independent things to go right at once, namely sustained mid-teens EDA growth, Ansys cross-sell and an IP recovery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Synopsys is valued as one continuing business on its first full post-Ansys year, with equity compensation treated as a real cost, the share count held flat, and the 10bn of acquisition debt deducted once. The flows are unlevered and exclude acquired-intangible amortisation and the FY2026 restructuring; the margin path is built from the guided non-GAAP operating margin rather than from a reported FCF margin that carries interest, restructuring cash and working-capital timing. The house and street values bracket the accounting choice on equity compensation, which for a company paying ~13% of revenue in stock and withholding taxes is the largest single swing factor in the valuation.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity-compensation basis: the house path charges 12.7% of revenue falling to 9.0%; charging the SBC expense alone (9.8% today) would lift every scenario materially
Base year is guidance, not actuals: FY2026 results are due 8 December 2026
Cash tax rate of 23% on post-SBC EBIT is an estimate; the company's non-GAAP rate is ~16% on a pre-SBC base
Terminal value is roughly two-thirds of enterprise value; a 1pp change in WACC moves the base case by about 15-20%
Design IP trajectory and China export controls are binary-ish inputs that the three scenarios bracket but cannot price precisely
Net debt is as at 31 July 2026 and excludes Q4 cash generation and any Q4 buybacks
